meta.title: An Empirical Decision Model for Selective Carbon-Aware Scheduling in CI/CD Pipelines Using Commit-Level Software Engineering Characteristics
meta.author: K. P. S. Nimsara
meta.guide_role: Documentation, not governance. If this guide disagrees with planning/PROGRESS.md or governance/03_DECISION_LOG.md, those files win (DL-025).

central_question.plain: Carbon-aware CI delays some builds until the electricity grid is cleaner. That saves carbon but slows developer feedback. The obvious way to pick which builds to delay is by how long they are expected to take, because a long build wastes more carbon when it runs at a dirty hour. This research asks whether knowing more about the commit itself (how big the change is, which files it touches, the project's history, the team) helps pick better builds than the expected duration alone.
central_question.technical: Do commit-time software-engineering (SE) characteristics provide material additional decision value, beyond a causal commit-time estimate of build duration (d-hat), for selecting which Stage-1-eligible CI builds enter carbon-aware deferral? Tested at model level (predeclared ΔPR-AUC floor vs the {d-hat} arm) and at decision level (frontier dominance of strategy 5 over 4a and 4b in the (carbon saved, TTFF p95) plane at matched operating points).

rqs.text: Which commit-level SE characteristics provide meaningful decision information for selective carbon-aware scheduling?
rqs.status: answered (P3-T5, revised under DL-034): no SE family shown to carry decision information beyond d-hat; F1 is an unresolved candidate (non-replicating, floor-sensitive, below the floor in the late test period, untested at the decision level)

rqs.text: Do commit-time SE characteristics provide meaningful additional decision value beyond a commit-time duration estimate for identifying builds suitable for carbon-aware scheduling?
rqs.status: answered (P3-T5, revised under DL-034): no, for the calibration-frozen policy (strategy 5 is identical to 4b and fails the decision condition at every floor); a frozen-policy null

rqs.text: How are the empirical findings (feature importance, ablation, effect sizes) transformed into an evidence-derived selective-scheduling policy?
rqs.status: answered: mechanical, reproducible fitting yields the duration-only spec (d480/w24), unchanged by the DL-034 correction; the SE-informed branch was never exercised

rqs.text: How effective is that policy against conventional CI scheduling, blanket carbon-aware scheduling and duration-only scheduling on identical replay traces?
rqs.status: answered (P3-T5, revised under DL-034): modest estimated carbon reduction vs immediate at a bounded feedback cost; far lower feedback cost than blanket carbon-aware; identical to 4b

propositions.text: A causal commit-time duration estimate plus the Stage-1 gate is sufficient: adding SE families does not clear the predeclared materiality floors.
propositions.note: The repository does not write formal H0/H1 statements. It predeclares a decision rule (eval_protocol.md §A1.7). This hypothesis wording is the guide's paraphrase of that rule.

propositions.text: At least one SE family clears the model-level floor (ΔPR-AUC CI excludes 0 and ≥ +0.01) AND strategy 5's frontier dominates both 4a and 4b by ≥ 5% relative TTFF p95 at matched carbon, or ≥ 1% relative carbon at matched TTFF p95, at ≥ 3 matched points.
propositions.note: Both altitudes must hold for admission (§A1.7). Every rule is re-run at ×0.5 and ×2 of both floors.

tasks.name: Carbon-intensity data acquisition

tasks.inputs: {{evidence.carbon.provider}}.
tasks.outputs: Hourly series + {{evidence.carbon.slots}}-slot profile in code/data/carbon/ with PROVENANCE.md; scheduler_core/carbon.py.

tasks.evidence: The protocol file itself: no TBD, and A1 appended without editing §§1–12.
tasks.why: Predeclaration is what makes a null result credible. The floors and rules cannot be moved after a result is seen.
tasks.plan_heading: Lock the evaluation protocol

tasks.name: Duration-control design specification
tasks.purpose: Define exactly what 'expected build duration' means before building it. It is the null hypothesis of the whole study.
tasks.inputs: eval_protocol.md §A1.1/§A1.2.
tasks.outputs: context/duration_control_spec.md: the d-hat definition, the information available at decision time, cut-off rules, forms 4a/4b, cold-start ladder, and leakage tests T1–T5. Design only: no code, no numbers.
tasks.decisions: DL-014 (accepted 2026-08-17): fitted parameters come from train projects only; 4b may read the scored project's own strictly-earlier builds on any split.
tasks.evidence: The spec file; the DL-014 resolution.
tasks.why: If the control is weak, SE features look useful by default. A strong, causal control is what makes the comparison fair.
tasks.plan_heading: Duration-control design specification (design only — no model code)

Frozen at sha256 {{evidence.splits.sha256|short}}….

tasks.purpose: Implement the duration control in both forms, prove it is causal, and choose the primary form by a predeclared rule.

tasks.outputs: scheduler_core/duration_estimator.py; fit id {{evidence.duration.fit_id}}; primary form 4b (expanding per-project prior).

tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P1-T4.passed}} tests passed; five leakage checks PASS; Spearman ρ 4b {{evidence.duration.f4b.rho|f3}} vs 4a {{evidence.duration.f4a.rho|f3}}; project-rung coverage {{evidence.duration.coverage_project_pct}}%.

tasks.name: Train, tune & calibrate (control + SE arms)
tasks.purpose: Train the duration-only arm {d-hat} and the full arm {d-hat + 28 features} with three algorithms, and calibrate their probabilities.
tasks.inputs: Train split (tuning inside train only), calibration split (calibrator fitting), frozen d-hat.
tasks.outputs: 6 arms ({control, full} × {xgboost, logreg, random_forest}), all isotonic-calibrated.
tasks.decisions: DL-018 (search spaces, imbalance handling, 20-candidate budget, the two arms).
tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P1-T5.passed}} tests passed. Calibration PR-AUC, xgboost control {{evidence.models.arms.xgboost_control.pr_auc|f4}} vs full {{evidence.models.arms.xgboost_full.pr_auc|f4}}.
tasks.why: Training the null as a first-class model means the SE arms are compared against an equally tuned baseline, not a straw man.
tasks.plan_heading: Train, tune & calibrate the decision models

tasks.name: Feature-family ablation + SHAP (calibration)
tasks.purpose: Measure each family's incremental value on its own ({d-hat + Fi} vs {d-hat}), with paired-bootstrap confidence intervals, and explain the full model with SHAP.
tasks.inputs: Frozen P1-T5 arms; the same train/calibration split.
tasks.outputs: 6 family arms; results/p1/ablation/deltas.json; results/p1/shap/.
tasks.decisions: DL-019 (arms, paired bootstrap B = 1000, SHAP method, variance decomposition).
tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P1-T6.passed}} tests passed; all six ΔPR-AUC values are negative and every 95% CI lies below 0; no leave-one-out arm was triggered.
tasks.why: Testing the full feature set alone cannot show which group of characteristics carries value, if any. The ablation can.
tasks.plan_heading: Feature-family ablation + SHAP on the calibration split

tasks.plan_heading: Apply the admission rule → the model-level RQ2 answer

tasks.name: Stage-1 eligibility gate + independent validator
tasks.purpose: Decide which builds may be deferred at all, with deterministic rules and no ML, and audit that decision with a second, independent implementation.
tasks.inputs: gh_is_pr and git_branch for {{evidence.eligibility.gated|int}} train + calibration builds.
tasks.outputs: scheduler_core/eligibility.py; replay/validate_invariants.py. Deferrable by rule: {{evidence.eligibility.eligible|int}} ({{evidence.eligibility.eligible_pct|f2}}%).
tasks.decisions: DL-020: the gate approximates deferability and does not measure it. Classes (d) manual and (e) scheduled/nightly have no marker in the data.
tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P2-T1.passed}} tests passed; 0 disagreements over {{evidence.eligibility.pairs_checked|int}} distinct input pairs; 0 validator violations.
tasks.why: Risk is not urgency (invariant 1). Whether a build may wait must never be decided by a failure score.
tasks.plan_heading: Stage 1: rule-based eligibility gate + independent validator

tasks.name: Energy & carbon accounting
tasks.purpose: Turn a build's observed duration into estimated energy and carbon, after the decision has been made.
tasks.inputs: Build duration (accounting only), the carbon profile, the energy config.
tasks.outputs: scheduler_core/accounting.py; config/energy.json with P_avg = {{evidence.energy.p_avg_w}} W.

tasks.plan_heading: Energy & carbon accounting

tasks.name: decide() over policy_spec
tasks.purpose: Build the one shared decision function: Stage 1 first, then Stage 2 under a spec file, with no threshold hard-coded.
tasks.inputs: A build's commit-time fields, the carbon profile, a validated PolicySpec.
tasks.outputs: scheduler_core/policy.py; a quarantined bootstrap spec; five worked examples.
tasks.decisions: DL-022: PyYAML safe_load only, a closed schema, and a bootstrap spec that can never produce a reported number.
tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P2-T3.passed}} passed, {{evidence.tests.P2-T3.skipped}} skipped; decide() raises if handed tr_duration; an AST check finds no float literals other than 0.0 and 1.0.

tasks.name: Trace-driven replay simulator (six strategies)
tasks.purpose: Replay historical builds through all six strategies across a frozen sweep grid, on identical inputs, deterministically.
tasks.inputs: A seeded sample of 12,000 calibration builds; the frozen d-hat and risk model; the carbon profile.
tasks.outputs: replay/simulator.py; replay/sweep_grid.json (102 settings); a bootstrap-labelled sample run.
tasks.decisions: DL-023 (strategies operationalised; 2 = gated whole-week horizon and 6 = skip eligible builds only, both author decisions; grids frozen).
tasks.evidence: {{evidence.tests.P2-T4.passed}} passed; 0 violations over {{evidence.replay.validator.deferred|int}} deferrals; byte-identical rerun.
tasks.why: Comparing strategies on the same builds in the same order is what makes the comparison paired and fair.
tasks.plan_heading: Trace-driven replay simulator (six strategies)

tasks.plan_heading: Test-split model evaluation + confirmatory ablation + SHAP
tasks.inputs: The 12 frozen P1 arms, the frozen d̂ (fit id {{evidence.duration.fit_id}}), each arm's calibration-split τ, and the 170 test projects.

On test, F1 clears the model-level floor (ΔPR-AUC {{evidence.p3_model.families.F1.delta|s4}}) although it was rejected on calibration; the admitted set is not stable across the floor sweep. {{evidence.tests.P3-T1.passed}} tests passed.

tasks.purpose: Replay the full test trace through all six strategies with the frozen policy, and record every protocol metric.
tasks.plan_heading: Full replay across all six strategies (test trace)

tasks.name: Decision-level value: 4 vs 5 frontiers (headline RQ2)
tasks.purpose: Compare the frozen policy's swept frontier with both duration controls at matched operating points: the headline RQ2 test.
tasks.plan_heading: Decision-level incremental value: ④ vs ⑤ **frontiers** (the headline RQ2 test)
tasks.inputs: The P3-T2 test replay parts (sha256-verified), plus a §A1.10 oracle-duration arm replayed from the tracked test trace.

tasks.decisions: DL-029 fixed the frontier, matched-point, area, floor, band and oracle rules before any frontier number existed; its §1 numeric check was restated before any result.
tasks.evidence: ⑤ vs ④b area {{evidence.p3_decision.vs_4b.point|s4}}, so the SE-adds-value condition fails at every floor. ④b beats ④a by {{evidence.p3_decision.vs_4a.point|s4}} pp·h. {{evidence.tests.P3-T3.passed}} tests passed.
tasks.why: Carbon cannot carry SE value under this energy model (§A1.13), so the test compares feedback delay at matched carbon across whole frontiers rather than at one point.

tasks.name: Sensitivity sweeps
tasks.purpose: Test whether each finding survives the predeclared perturbations: eligibility rule, delay window, energy model, time period, cold starts, duration-control form, and a second grid.
tasks.plan_heading: Sensitivity analyses
tasks.inputs: The P3-T2 test replay, P3-T1 per-build scores, the tracked test trace, and (for the second grid) the public EIA-930 California series.
tasks.outputs: results/p3/sensitivity.md (the verdict table first) and one JSON per sweep; figure of the duration-control finding across sweeps.
tasks.decisions: DL-030 defined the sweeps and the four verdicts before any sweep ran; DL-031 switched the second-grid source to account-free EIA data; DL-032 recorded the second grid as not run (author decision).
tasks.evidence: Two predeclared flips, both reported prominently: one RQ4 class at a 12-hour window, and the duration-control counting rule in the late test period (area {{evidence.p3_sensitivity.v3_late_area|s4}}, direction unchanged). {{evidence.tests.P3-T4.passed}} tests passed.
tasks.why: A result that only holds at one setting is fragile. Defining what counts as a flip before running the sweeps keeps this test honest.

decisions.summary: Framework hardening: North-Star card, state files carry no instructions, derived task counts.

decisions.title: Add calibration-quality metrics to the RQ1 evaluation
decisions.summary: Calibration-quality metrics (Brier, ECE, reliability) added to RQ1 evaluation.

decisions.summary: Time-to-failure-feedback (TTFF) and missed-failure metrics added, so skip strategies are not flattered.

decisions.title: Three-way project-disjoint, time-ordered split (train / calibration / test)
decisions.summary: Three-way project-disjoint, time-ordered split: train / calibration / test.

decisions.title: Explicit, cited energy model with sensitivity band
decisions.summary: Explicit energy model E = P_avg × duration with a mandatory ±50% band; P_avg must be cited.

decisions.title: Pin the deferral-window mapping (the Stage-2 knob)
decisions.summary: Deferral window pinned: w(p) = W_max·(1−p), W_max = 24 h, sweep {6,12,24} + banded variant.

decisions.title: Model at build grain; the build-level aggregation rule
decisions.summary: Model at build grain; job rows aggregated by tr_build_id (duration by max).

decisions.title: Energy-model duration source = tr_duration (refines DL-007)
decisions.summary: Energy duration source is tr_duration (tr_log_buildduration is 95.3% null).

decisions.title: Opt-in commit-at-gate; commit messages carry no AI attribution
decisions.summary: Commits are opt-in at gates and never carry AI attribution.

decisions.title: Framework migration: selective carbon-aware scheduling; SE characteristics tested against a commit-time duration control
decisions.summary: Framework migration: the question becomes whether SE characteristics add value beyond a commit-time duration estimate. Six strategies; invariants 6–7 added; Layer 0-A created.

decisions.title: The decision-level test compares trade-off frontiers, not single points (corrects DL-012 §5)
decisions.summary: Decision-level test compares swept frontiers at matched operating points, not single points (carbon ∝ duration makes single-point comparison unsatisfiable).

decisions.title: What A1.1's information rule binds: fitted parameters vs. causal within-project state
decisions.summary: Fitted parameters from train projects only; 4b may read the scored project's own strictly-earlier builds on any split (the deployment information regime).

decisions.title: Feature-construction decisions: the num_commits source, four unbuildable §3.5 features, the missing-value policy, and a strengthened blocklist
decisions.summary: Feature construction: num_commits source chosen; change entropy and fix-keyword dropped; developer experience and subsystems proxied; missing-value policy; stronger blocklist.

decisions.title: git_diff_test_churn is entirely zero in this release: two contracted features are constant, and F1/F2/F3 are weakened
decisions.summary: git_diff_test_churn is zero in the whole release, so two features are constant and F1/F2/F3 are weakened.

decisions.title: The frozen split is heterogeneous by construction: base rate and duration differ across splits
decisions.summary: The frozen split is heterogeneous: failure rate and duration tail differ across splits (a measured threat, not a deviation).

decisions.title: P1-T5 training configuration: search spaces, imbalance handling, budget, and the two arms
decisions.summary: P1-T5 training configuration: search spaces, imbalance handling, 20-candidate budget, control and full arms.

decisions.title: P1-T6 ablation configuration: arms, paired-bootstrap procedure, SHAP method, variance decomposition
decisions.summary: P1-T6 ablation configuration: arms, paired bootstrap, SHAP method, variance decomposition, directional floor reading.

decisions.title: The Stage-1 eligibility gate is an experimental approximation of deferability, not a measurement of it
decisions.summary: The Stage-1 gate approximates deferability and does not measure it; manual and scheduled classes are absent; its error rate is unmeasurable.

decisions.title: P_avg_W is pinned at 42.5 W, cited from CodeCarbon's constant-mode CPU fallback (discharges DL-007's cite-or-log)
decisions.summary: P_avg = 42.5 W from CodeCarbon's constant-mode CPU fallback (85 W × 0.5), source pinned at v3.3.1.

decisions.title: PyYAML enters the §3.2 stack; the policy_spec.yaml schema contract; and the bootstrap spec may never produce a reported number
decisions.summary: PyYAML safe_load; closed policy_spec schema; the bootstrap spec can never produce a reported number.

decisions.title: The six strategies, operationally; the predeclared sweep grids; and what a replay record is
decisions.summary: The six strategies operationalised; sweep grids frozen (W, D, τ); replay record schema; determinism.

decisions.title: How fit_policy.py fixes the frozen operating point; policy_spec.yaml schema v2; replay characteristics carried into P3
decisions.summary: Operating point fixed by predeclared carbon retention (ρ = 0.90); schema v2; frozen 12k sample; 4b primary kept; replay characteristics documented.

decisions.title: A living research guide is regenerated at every gate; it is documentation, never governance
decisions.summary: This research guide is regenerated from results/ at every gate; it is documentation, never governance, and reports discrepancies rather than fixing them.

decisions.title: Proposed P4 artifact direction: carbon-aware CI decision support as a reusable GitHub Action (conditional on P3)
decisions.summary: Proposed/Conditional P4 direction: a reusable GitHub Action giving RUN NOW / DEFER recommendations with region and forecast awareness. It changes nothing in P3 and must be confirmed after P3-T5.

decisions.title: Two predeclared P3-T4 sensitivities: a within-corpus temporal robustness sweep and a second, higher-variance grid profile
decisions.summary: Two P3-T4 sensitivities predeclared before test opened: an early/late temporal split at a fixed boundary, and a second higher-variance grid (CAISO, then Germany), reported for RQ4 ranking invariance only.

decisions.title: The P3-T1 F1 finding is reported, not acted on; test_scores.csv.gz is tracked; P3-T2's headline operating points and replay method, predeclared
decisions.summary: Option (a): the F1 test finding is reported, with no post-hoc F1 arm; test_scores.csv.gz tracked; RQ4 headline operating points, streaming replay and the paired bootstrap predeclared before the test replay.

decisions.title: How P3-T3's frontier test is computed: frontiers, matched points, area, floors, bands, oracle
decisions.summary: Operational rules for the P3-T3 frontier test (Pareto frontier, 10 interior matched points, area, §A1.7 counting, bands, oracle), fixed before any frontier number existed.

decisions.title: How P3-T4's sensitivity sweeps are run, and what "the verdict flips" means
decisions.summary: Nine predeclared sensitivity sweeps and the four verdicts (V1–V4) that 'stable / flips' is judged on, fixed before any sweep ran.

decisions.title: S-f's CAISO series comes from EIA-930, not Electricity Maps (source change, before any S-f result)
decisions.summary: Second-grid source switched to the public, account-free EIA-930 California series (consumed intensity, lb→g, hour-end → hour-start), before the profile was built.

decisions.title: S-f (second grid) is reported as not run: no qualifying zone under DL-027 §2
decisions.summary: Second grid reported as not run: California was not more variable than the UK, and Germany had no account-free series (author decision).

decisions.title: The DL-026 follow-up: P4 becomes a duration-history carbon-deferral advisor that embodies the P3 null (amends DL-026; proposed amendment to spec §5 and P4-T1..T3)
decisions.summary: Accepted 2026-10-04 (revision 3). P4 is a duration-based CI deferral advisor: shared decide() + GitHub Action + REST API + Repo What-If Report (replaces the dashboard). No SE features, SHAP or risk score; completed-run history only; GB only with a declared compute location; recommendation-first; fail-safe RUN NOW; What-If is demonstration only.

decisions.title: ④b's history admits only builds that had finished before the scored build arrived; the full evidence chain is re-run under this entry (corrects DL-014 §Resolution 2)
decisions.summary: An independent review found the duration control counted builds still running. Fixed and re-ran P1 to P3 under predeclared rules (author option a). No RQ verdict changed; F1's late-period admission and strategy 6's mid-tau ordering did.

decisions.title: P4-T1 implementation decisions: two stack additions, line-ending-normalised pins, and four contract details
decisions.summary: uvicorn and httpx join the stack; the advisor pins LF-normalised hashes (the profile's CRLF working-copy hash would never match on Linux); repo_language, a wall-clock duration default with a budgeted timing lookup, an API that never fetches history, scenario mode as a request field, and is_pr accepted as the Stage-1 input.

decisions.title: P4-T2: a GitHub-hosted runner replaces the East US VM as the real non-GB case; the Action's runtime dependencies; how the Action is published
decisions.summary: No self-hosted runner: public repositories run free on GitHub-hosted runners, and GitHub advises against self-hosted runners on public repositories. The real case declares GITHUB-HOSTED and fails safe; GB DEFER comes from labelled scenario mode. The Action installs a 12-package subset pinned to the lockfile, with --no-deps. The demo workload is synthetic. The Action was pushed before the gate so the demo could pin its SHA.

limitations.claim: SE characteristics are universally useless for CI scheduling
limitations.detail: Only the tested operationalisation (28 features, 6 families, one algorithm budget) was found null, on calibration so far. F2 is half dead (DL-016); commit messages and change entropy are unavailable (DL-015).

limitations.claim: The tested SE families add material model-level value beyond d-hat
limitations.detail: All six families were rejected on calibration (CIs below 0). On test only F1 clears the floor; it does not replicate, is empty at x2, and falls below the floor in the late test period (P3-T1, P3-T4, DL-034).

limitations.claim: SE characteristics add decision-level value (frontier dominance)
limitations.detail: Under the frozen duration-only spec, strategy 5 is identical to 4b, so the decision test is null by construction. F1's decision-level value was never tested (DL-028 section 1).
At most it can be shown adequate or not materially beaten under this protocol. Many signals and mechanisms remain untested.

limitations.claim: The study measures real production emissions
limitations.detail: Carbon is estimated from constant 42.5 W × duration × an hour-of-week mean intensity. No energy is measured.

limitations.claim: Builds classed deferrable were actually safe to delay
limitations.detail: No ground-truth deferability or urgency label exists in TravisTorrent (DL-020). Eligibility is an experimental population.

limitations.claim: Results transfer to GitHub Actions or modern CI
limitations.detail: Travis CI, 2011–2016, four languages; spec §6 declares that generalisation is not claimed.

limitations.claim: The carbon profile describes when the builds actually ran
limitations.detail: The UK 2024–2025 profile is aligned by hour-of-week to 2011–2016 arrivals. It is a scenario, not a reconstruction.

limitations.claim: The carbon channel can show SE value
limitations.detail: Carbon saved is proportional to duration by construction (§A1.13), so RQ2's power rests on TTFF.

limitations.claim: IP geolocation identifies the data centre
limitations.detail: Not in the plan. If added it can only give an estimated region.

limitations.claim: The artifact is operationally reliable at production scale
limitations.detail: P4 is not started; re-dispatch, retries, cancellations and concurrency are undemonstrated.

limitations.claim: The chosen operating point is robust
limitations.detail: It is fitted on a 12k sample of calibration builds and is ρ-sensitive: ρ 0.80 gives d240/w12 (TTFF p95 {{evidence.policy.sensitivity.0.ttff_p95_h|f2}} h vs {{evidence.policy.chosen_ttff_p95_h|f2}} h).

change_history.event: Phase 0 complete: M0 (data harness, carbon series, frozen protocol).
Reframing (DL-012): value-of-information study; plan 22 → 28 tasks; DL-013 corrects the decision-level test before any code.
Phase 1 complete: M1. Model-level RQ2 answer on calibration: null path.
Phase 2 complete: M2. policy_spec.yaml fitted and frozen (duration-only, 480 s, 24 h). Test split still closed.
Research guide created (docs/research_guide.html, DL-025). First version; reflects 16/28.

P3-T1 gated. Test split opened once. F1 clears the model-level floor on test but not on calibration, and not at ×2 of the floor; the frozen duration-only policy is unchanged. DL-026 and DL-027 recorded before opening.
P3-T2 gated. Full test trace replayed once through all six strategies with the frozen policy; 0 gate violations; headline rows fixed in advance by DL-028.
P3-T3 gated. Decision-level RQ2: the frozen policy (≡ ④b) realises no SE decision value; ④b's frontier dominates ④a's; the oracle bound shows headroom in duration estimation.

P3-T4 gated. Sensitivity sweeps run; RQ2 decision verdict unchanged by construction; RQ4 pattern stable except one class at a 12-hour window; duration-control finding keeps its direction everywhere; second grid not run (DL-032).

P3-T5 gated. Evaluation report written; all four RQs answered. RQ1/RQ2 null (F1 a non-replicating model-level candidate), RQ3 duration-only spec, RQ4 modest and robust in sign. Phase 3 complete. P4 waits on the DL-026 follow-up decision.

CR-1 (DL-034) gated. Duration history corrected to finished builds only; P1 to P3 re-run under predeclared rules. No RQ verdict changed; F1's late-period admission flipped to empty and strategy 6 now beats 5 on estimated carbon at mid tau. Evaluation report revised.

DL-033 revision 3 accepted. P4 re-scoped to a duration-based CI deferral advisor with a GitHub Action, a REST API and a Repo What-If Report in place of the dashboard; GB only, recommendation-first, fail-safe RUN NOW. Plan P4-T1..T3 rewritten; still 28 tasks.

P4-T1 gated: the advisor core, completed-run history adapter, CLI and REST API run the frozen decide() unchanged; 763 tests pass; real API and real GitHub-history captures recorded as demonstration evidence (DL-035).

P4-T2 gated: the composite GitHub Action runs the advisor in CI. Seven runs on the public demo repository: cold start, protected branch, GB-scenario DEFER, urgent veto, two fail-safes, pull_request_target refused; audit log 0 violations; 789 tests pass. A GitHub-hosted runner replaces the East US VM; re-dispatch cut (DL-036).
